chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had three wives, and he married two more women to them in a single contract. He consummated the marriage with one of them, then he died. He said: 'If he had consummated the marriage with the woman he began with by name and mentioned her at the time of the marriage contract, then her marriage is valid, she is entitled to inheritance, and she must observe the waiting period.' He said: 'And if he had consummated the marriage with the one who was mentioned after the mention of the first, then her marriage is invalid, she has no inheritance, but she is entitled to the dowry she received in exchange for what she made permissible of her private part, and she must observe the waiting period.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on multiple wives under one contract when the husband dies after consummating with only one?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the principle of 'explicit designation' (takhassus) in simultaneous polygamous contracts, a key issue in Usuli jurisprudence regarding the validity of multiple marriages at once. The distinction hinges on whether the man specified the first wife by name during the contract formation, thereby validating her status for inheritance and waiting period (iddah), while rendering the subsequent unnamed unions void unless consummated. This highlights the Shia emphasis on precise contractual intent (niyyah and declaration) over mere physical act in determining legal consequences.
